title: I remember only ideas and sensations.
html_source: As he does frequently, Mulligan dodges responsibility for his hurtful remarks by relying on philosophical jargon. In this remark Buck echoes two 18th-century philosophers: the English empiricist John Locke and the Irish idealist Bishop George Berkeley. Both of them wrote that all knowledge (and thus all memory, as Buck would have it) comes only from man’s physical sensation of external stimuli, and subsequently the ideas formed in our mind based on those sensations. Stephen will ponder these philosophies at the beginning of chapter 3, “Proteus”.
